reminder.notes:
Reliability fixes from the v2.19.61 two-device logs

### Features
- The diagnostics log now records the exact time each alarm was armed for, a one-line roster of every armed reminder and its next fire time after each reconcile, and a line each time the background worker starts. A missed reminder can now be traced to whether this device was holding an alarm for that moment at all.
- Duplicate copies of a LAN message are dropped on arrival. Each action was sent three times for reliability and applied three times on the receiving phone.

### Bug fixes
- Location reminders are no longer reported as having a missing alarm on every check. The check could only see clock alarms, so a perfectly healthy geofence was re-armed endlessly and the health counter permanently showed a failure that was not there.
- Instant Wi-Fi sync of reminder edits between phones now works. It was sending the entire database in one message on every change, which was far too large to fit, so nothing was ever delivered over Wi-Fi and every edit waited for the cloud.
- Snoozing or completing a reminder no longer loses track of the alarm it just set. The app could hold an alarm it did not know about, so a reminder deleted or completed on the other phone could still ring here.

ai-scanner.notes:
AI Scanner 1.4.1 — Background update checks, and no more double-downloading updates

### Features
- AI Scanner now checks for updates periodically in the background (about every 6 hours) and posts a notification when one is found, in addition to the existing manual "Check for Updates" in Settings. Tapping the notification opens the app; the download and install still happen from the Settings sheet.

### Bug fixes
- The update downloader now persists its in-flight DownloadManager id and re-attaches to a still-running download instead of deleting the partial file and starting over — fixes re-downloading the same update from zero after backgrounding or reopening the app mid-update.
- The update sheet now re-syncs its progress on resume instead of occasionally showing a frozen progress bar.

No user-facing bug fixes in this release.

localsender.notes:
Local Sender 1.0.11 - security hardening (full audit)

A full security audit (see AUDIT.md and THREAT_MODEL.md in the repo) and fixes for
every CRITICAL and HIGH finding it turned up. All local content is now encrypted
at rest, the macOS build is sandboxed again, and Drive backup no longer stores its
own key next to the data it protects.

### Features
- Google Drive backup is now sealed with a passphrase you set and never upload —
  Drive alone can no longer read a backup, only you can.
- A warning dialog when a device presents a different identity key than the one
  already trusted under that name, instead of an ordinary pairing prompt.

### Bug fixes
- Chat history, rooms, trusted-peer keys, peer profiles, network profiles, and
  device name are now encrypted at rest (previously plaintext in local storage).
- Fixed a path-traversal bug where an incoming file offer's name could write
  outside the downloads folder.
- Fixed an unbounded network frame length that let any device on the LAN push
  memory usage toward the app's limit with a single unauthenticated connection.
- A silent, unresponsive peer during pairing could lock the app out of pairing
  with anyone else; pairing now times out and recovers.
- A connection dropped mid-file-transfer no longer leaves a frozen progress row
  or an orphaned partial file on disk.
- Re-enabled the macOS App Sandbox (previously off since v1.0.1 to work around a
  Keychain hang); the underlying hang is now handled by an existing timeout and
  fallback, so sandboxing no longer breaks pairing.
- The identity key's on-disk fallback file (used only when the OS secure store is
  unavailable) is now encrypted instead of holding the raw key.

bchat.notes:
BChat 0.3.0-beta.2 — files up to 50 MB, sessions that survive a restart

Install this over 0.3.0-beta.1. It fixes a defect in that build serious enough
that beta.1 should not be used: conversations silently ended every time the app
was closed.

The relay still listens only on the Tailscale network. A phone that is not on
that network cannot send or receive.

### Features

- Attachments up to 50 MB. Files are encrypted with a key of their own, uploaded
  to the server in resumable 1 MB pieces, and announced in a message carrying
  the id and the key. The server stores bytes it cannot read, and a large upload
  no longer blocks messages behind it.
- The size limit is checked when you pick the file, not after it uploads, so an
  oversized file costs you no data.
- A new app icon. The old one was a Bluetooth rune, which described a transport
  the app no longer has.

### Bug fixes

- Sessions are now kept on disk. In beta.1 they lived only in memory, so closing
  the app silently ended every conversation until both phones re-handshaked, and
  anything that arrived in between could not be decrypted. The app looked like
  it was working the whole time. This is the reason to install this build.
- Ratchet state is written before a message is sent, so a crash between the two
  cannot cause a message key to be reused.
- Stored session state that will not load is discarded rather than partly
  restored, because continuing under a half-loaded ratchet reuses message keys.
- Onboarding still offered "chat over Bluetooth, no internet, no SIM", and media
  still talked about waiting to share Wi-Fi. Both described the old app.

### Known gaps in this build

- Notifications still do not arrive while the app is closed. This needs push,
  which needs a Firebase project that has to be created interactively.
- The server is not reachable from the open internet yet.
- Multi-device linking, username sign-in and encrypted backup are built and
  tested on the server but have no screens.
- Groups work on the server but have no client side.
